articles.headline: La reunión por el matadero de Sarria acaba sin fecha ni compromisos
articles.subtitle: Carniceros y ganaderos propusieron reactivar de inmediato las líneas de vacuno y porcino antes del grueso de la campaña de matanzas; el gobierno local no fijó calendario ni partidas.
articles.body:
El Concello de Sarria y los profesionales del sector celebraron este martes una reunión sobre el matadero municipal que concluyó sin fecha ni compromisos para su reapertura. El alcalde, Claudio Garrido, y la concejala responsable del servicio, Geni Valcárcel, escucharon las demandas de carniceros y ganaderos.

El matadero lleva seis meses cerrado por varias averías, una situación que el sector considera especialmente preocupante por la llegada de las matanzas tradicionales. Los profesionales propusieron al gobierno local reactivar inmediatamente la línea de sacrificio de vacuno y la de porcino antes del grueso de la campaña, y reclamaron una respuesta urgente.

Los ganaderos llevan semanas pidiendo explicaciones al Concello y el pleno ya aprobó por unanimidad reparar la instalación para impulsar su reapertura. Sin calendario ni partidas confirmadas tras el encuentro, el sector advierte de que la campaña de invierno depende de que las líneas vuelvan a funcionar.

articles.headline: El paro sube en 95.900 personas pese al récord de 22,8 millones de ocupados
articles.subtitle: La agricultura perdió 58.300 empleos y la población activa creció en 169.500 personas; Economía se apoya en el dato desestacionalizado, con 70.000 ocupados más y 25 trimestres de avances.
articles.body:
La Encuesta de Población Activa del tercer trimestre deja un balance flojo: el paro aumentó en 95.900 personas mientras el empleo alcanzó un nuevo récord de 22,8 millones de ocupados, con 73.600 puestos más que en el trimestre anterior. La población activa subió en 169.500 personas hasta 25,4 millones, el máximo de la serie.

El Ministerio de Economía destaca la creación de empleo en términos desestacionalizados, que considera la medida más fiable: 70.000 ocupados más y 25 trimestres consecutivos de avances. El departamento insiste además en que la ocupación marca máximos históricos y en que el aumento de la población activa explica buena parte del repunte del paro.

El campo es el sector más castigado. La agricultura destruyó 58.300 puestos de trabajo y sumó 18.000 parados más, un desplome que coincide con la protesta de Asaja, COAG y Unión de Uniones en Madrid. Los servicios, en cambio, sostuvieron la creación de empleo durante el trimestre y compensaron la atonía del resto de ramas.

articles.headline: Medio millar de tractores cerca Madrid para exigir un plan de choque para el campo
articles.subtitle: Asaja, COAG y Unión de Uniones, sin UPA, avanzan desde cinco puntos hasta el Ministerio de Agricultura bajo el lema «Por un campo con futuro», el mismo día en que la EPA destruye 58.300 empleos agrarios.
articles.body:
Cinco columnas formadas por medio millar de tractores confluyeron este miércoles en la plaza de Colón para marchar después hacia la sede del Ministerio de Agricultura, Pesca y Alimentación. Las marchas partieron de El Espinar, Buitrago de Lozoya, Guadalajara, Torrejón de la Calzada y Arganda del Rey.

Bajo el lema «Por un campo con futuro», Asaja, COAG y Unión de Uniones, con la ausencia de UPA, reclaman un plan de choque frente a la escalada de costes y exigen participar en el diseño de la futura PAC. Los productores cifran en 200 millones de euros el sobrecoste de la sementera y denuncian que casi la mitad del sector se ha quedado sin las ayudas a los fertilizantes.

La protesta coincidió con la publicación de la EPA del tercer trimestre, que refleja un castigo severo para el sector primario: la agricultura perdió 58.300 ocupados y sumó 18.000 parados, justo cuando arranca la campaña de siembra. Las organizaciones sostienen que el encarecimiento de los insumos y la falta de ayudas dejan sin margen a las explotaciones más pequeñas.

articles.headline: La jueza del caso Ceuta reprocha al CNI una colaboración «escueta»
articles.subtitle: El juzgado considera «esencial» interrogar a dos agentes del centro; Interior sostiene que no hubo aviso de un «riesgo real» y que la entrada masiva «no era previsible».
articles.body:
La jueza que instruye el caso de la entrada masiva de migrantes en Ceuta reprochó al Centro Nacional de Inteligencia una colaboración «escueta» y consideró «esencial» interrogar a dos de sus agentes, según las diligencias conocidas este martes. El juzgado quiere precisar qué información manejaba el servicio secreto sobre la concentración previa en la frontera.

En paralelo, el Ministerio del Interior trasladó a la instructora que no recibió avisos de un «riesgo real» y que la entrada «no era previsible». Los consejeros ceutíes que declararon como testigos describieron en cambio una entrada organizada y una cierta pasividad de los gendarmes marroquíes, una versión que matiza la del departamento.

La petición se suma a la declaración de los dos mandos que comparecieron la semana pasada y que, según sus propios relatos, no recibieron orden de cerrar la valla. El interrogatorio de los agentes del CNI determinará ahora si la causa se amplía hacia el ámbito de la inteligencia o se queda en la cadena de mando policial.

articles.headline: Suspicious package at Derry's Ebrington Square prompts security alert
articles.subtitle: Police were called at about 15:20 on Tuesday after the package was found at the Waterside site, where a Halloween funfair is running; a business premises was evacuated and no roads were closed.
articles.body:
Police are dealing with a security alert at Ebrington Square in the Waterside area of Londonderry after a suspicious package was discovered at about 15:20 on Tuesday. A nearby business premises has been evacuated. No roads are closed, and the Peace Bridge linking Ebrington to the city centre remains open.

A Halloween funfair at the site is operating as normal. DUP MLA Julie Middleton said on social media that it was not yet known whether the package was "a legitimate threat, a hoax, a mistaken item or otherwise", adding: "Very worrying nonetheless."

Waterside Ulster Unionist councillor Darren Guy told BBC News NI that he hoped the alert would end soon, saying it was causing disruption for the businesses affected and for the many families attending the funfair, and that it was not what the city should be dealing with in the week of its Halloween festival.

The Executive Office, which owns the Ebrington site, said it was aware of the ongoing situation and asked the public to follow police advice. The PSNI said an update would be provided in due course.

articles.headline: Finland and Norway hold a rare joint call with Putin on ending the war
articles.subtitle: The 90-minute call from Helsinki was «frank and substantive», Alexander Stubb said, and the Kremlin said Putin blamed «confrontational» EU and NATO policy for prolonging the war in Ukraine.
articles.body:
The leaders of Finland and Norway held a joint call with Vladimir Putin on Tuesday, a rare direct contact between the Russian president and European leaders. The aim, their offices said, was to look at future negotiations to help end the war in Ukraine, and they stressed the initiative was not taken on behalf of Europe as a whole.

The 90-minute call was made from Helsinki and showed "big differences in views", according to Norway's prime minister, Jonas Gahr Støre. President Alexander Stubb said the conversation was "frank and substantive" and argued that the outcome of the war will have a direct impact on Finnish, Nordic and wider European security.

The Kremlin said Putin told the two leaders that a "just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered, and that he blamed confrontational EU and NATO policies for prolonging the war. All three agreed to continue their direct phone communication.

Volodymyr Zelensky spoke to both leaders afterwards and thanked them for their "active support", having met them and the US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo last week. Last weekend the Kremlin spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, said having a European negotiator at the peace table would be "good".

articles.headline: Jordan strikes targets in Syria over the church funeral attack, then the border reopens
articles.subtitle: Syrian health officials said five people, including women and children, were killed in a Daraa village; Damascus shut the Nassib crossing in response and reopened it on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Jordanian fighter jets struck what the kingdom's military called "terrorist organisations" in southern Syria on Monday, in retaliation for the shooting at a Greek Orthodox church funeral in Karak on Friday that killed nine people and wounded 34. Jordan said its aircraft killed and wounded "several terrorists" without giving further details.

Syrian health officials told state media that five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed in a village in Daraa province; Al Jazeera put the toll at seven. Jordan said the strikes had been co-ordinated with the Syrian government, while Damascus said it had not been notified.

Syria closed the Nassib crossing, the only passenger and commercial link between the two countries, then announced it would reopen on Wednesday morning with traffic resuming in both directions. The two foreign ministries formed a security committee to share intelligence and follow up on the impact of the strikes.

Jordanian security forces arrested two brothers and their brother-in-law on suspicion of carrying out the church attack, which ISIL claimed. Damascus said it had opened direct channels of communication with Amman and launched "comprehensive investigations" into the targeting.

articles.headline: Trump showcases a tanker of Venezuelan oil at a Texas rally
articles.subtitle: Speaking in Corpus Christi on his fourth trip to Texas this campaign season, the president pointed to the Angerona and said it held a million barrels, with two rallies staged to defend a Senate seat.
articles.body:
Donald Trump used a campaign stop in Corpus Christi, Texas, on Tuesday to draw attention to a crude oil tanker docked nearby, the Angerona, which he said was carrying a million barrels of Venezuelan oil. He held two rallies in the state in a single day, his fourth visit there this campaign season.

The visit was intended to underscore the administration's military operation in Latin America at a moment when the war with Iran has turned affordability into the dominant issue of the midterms. Texas hosts one of the races that will decide control of the Senate.

Trump and his allies have attacked the Democratic candidate, the state representative James Talarico, as too "radical" for Texas, with the attorney general, Ken Paxton, seeking to portray his policies as hostile to a state built on business. Trump urged supporters to vote as if he were on the ballot.

"If you go out, and if you all vote, we win in a landslide," he told the crowd. The administration has made Latin America a centrepiece of its foreign policy, and the Venezuelan oil shipment has become its most visible prop on the campaign trail.

articles.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro flees to the US to seek asylum after his election defeat
articles.subtitle: The defeated candidate left Brazil on a private jet with his family instead of surrendering his passports to the supreme court, hours after Lula turned 81 with a warning about those who «flee in secret».
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil for the United States with his family on Tuesday and intends to request political asylum, two days after losing the presidential runoff to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva by 51.78% to 48.22%. He had promised to lead the opposition to the Workers' Party government.

Rather than hand over his passports as a supreme court judge had ordered, the senator boarded a private jet, avoiding what appeared to be an imminent arrest in two investigations against him. The Trump administration granted the visas needed to enter the country.

Simon Levy, a Mexican lawyer with influence in Trump's circle, attributed the operation's design to the secretary of state, Marco Rubio: "He is the brain behind this operation." Much of Bolsonaro's own camp was said to be unaware of the plan until he was already in the air.

Lula marked his 81st birthday with a blunt message for his former rival. "The citizen who flees his country in secret does so because he owes something or is afraid of something," he said. "I regret the lack of respect he has shown towards his voters and towards democracy."

articles.headline: Mbappé loses his Chinese sponsors over a Mao Zedong joke
articles.subtitle: Dongpeng and Mengniu ended all cooperation with the Real Madrid forward within hours of a video circulating online, as the row topped Weibo a day after he missed out on the Ballon d'Or.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappé was dropped by two major brands in China on Tuesday after a video circulated online in which the France and Real Madrid forward appeared to joke about the former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. The drinks group Dongpeng said it was terminating all cooperation with immediate effect.

"Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments," Dongpeng said in a statement. Mengniu, China's largest dairy producer, also cut ties, using near-identical language to announce that it was ending all cooperation with the player at once.

"Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe" was the top trending topic on the social media platform Weibo. The 27-year-old had lost out to Harry Kane for the Ballon d'Or a day earlier, and apologised for the remark in a message in which he said he had hurt many people.

Commercial deals in China carry political risk for European footballers, and brands there move quickly when a campaign threatens to become a nationalist row. Neither Dongpeng nor Mengniu indicated whether the rupture was temporary, and Mbappé's club has not commented.

articles.headline: Apple puts the M6 in the MacBook Pro and the iMac, a day before its Pro and Tell event
articles.subtitle: The 14-inch MacBook Pro starts at $1,999 with 24 hours of battery life, Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6; Apple claims the chip is up to 30% faster at graphics and 25% faster on AI workloads than the M5.
articles.body:
Apple refreshed the 14-inch MacBook Pro and the iMac with its new M6 chip on Tuesday, a day before a "Pro and Tell" event at which further hardware is expected. The laptop starts at $1,999 in space black and silver, and the iMac at $1,499 in seven colours.

The M6 pairs a 12-core CPU, which Apple calls the world's fastest CPU core, with a 12-core GPU that it says is up to 30% faster at graphics and up to 25% faster on AI workloads than the M5. Apple also claims up to 13 times the prompt-processing speed of an M1 MacBook Pro.

The laptop ships with 16GB of unified memory, configurable to 32GB, and memory bandwidth rises to 170GB/s from 153GB/s on the M5. Ports are unchanged: HDMI, MagSafe 3, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, an SDXC slot and a headphone jack. Fast charging reaches 50% in 30 minutes.

The iMac's M6 adds Neural Accelerators to every core, which Apple says helps with multitasking, photo editing and video work. The iPad mini was updated on Monday, and the company has been clearing space in the line-up ahead of Wednesday's event.

articles.headline: iFixit says the iPhone Duo's hinge is pressing into its inner screen
articles.subtitle: Owners began posting photos of cracks and black spots above the fold within hours of Friday's launch; Apple has acknowledged an "issue" and is replacing damaged units without saying how many.
articles.body:
Within hours of the iPhone Duo going on sale on Friday, owners reported that the inner screen on some brand new foldables was already broken. The damage looked similar across the photos shared online: a crack or defect in the middle of the display above the hinge, with lines running down the right side.

Shahram Mokhtari, the lead teardown technician at iFixit, told The Verge that the cause appears to lie in the hinge, where gears, springs and joints let the device close flat while giving the screen room to bend gently. At the trouble spot, the flexible inner screen is pushing up against part of the hinge.

That panel is "extremely sensitive", he said: poke at its edges with a pick or a sharp tool and "you're going to break that screen". In the damaged units the black spot tends to sit exactly where the metal is meeting the display, which fits the theory better than simple user error.

Apple acknowledged the issue on Monday and said it is replacing affected phones, without saying how many have been reported. A repair programme on a device this new is expensive, and the cause matters: if the hinge is at fault, replacing screens alone may not settle it.

articles.headline: Tailscale races out patches for 11 flaws in its SSH server and connectors
articles.subtitle: Cyberdione Labs found the bugs, collectively called Tailworm, while auditing Tailscale 1.104.2 and the headscale control server; the worst can give an already-authorised user root on a host.
articles.body:
Tailscale is patching almost a dozen vulnerabilities that could be used to steal credentials, crash servers and gain root privileges, after a security audit of its mesh VPN software. Cyberdione Labs found the 11 flaws, collectively named Tailworm, in Tailscale 1.104.2 and the self-hosted headscale 0.29.5 control server.

The most serious sits in Tailscale SSH, the SSH server embedded in tailscaled, which runs as root. Unix-socket forwarding performs path checks and file operations with root privileges, and races plus a missing privilege drop let an ordinary session replace, dial or delete privileged resources.

Exploiting it needs one approved device and one SSH policy rule, and on headscale forwarding is granted automatically. Other findings cover the experimental app connectors, which can reach cloud metadata and internal networks without consulting access rules, an unauthenticated resource-exhaustion bug in headscale, and the DERP relay client.

Erica Windisch, who founded Cyberdione Labs, said all findings were reproduced against unmodified released software and that the flaws were found "with low effort". Tailscale said it received the report on Monday and was working on patches, and that it does not recommend everyone disable Tailscale SSH.

articles.headline: Discord will make messages from its public servers searchable on the web
articles.subtitle: From 16 November every Discoverable Server gets its own page, and from mid-December selected public messages may surface in search results; members can opt out and usernames are not shown.
articles.body:
Discord said on Tuesday that conversations in some of its public servers will become searchable and easier to find on the open web. The change covers "Discoverable Servers", the public communities whose administrators have made them eligible to appear in Discord's Server Discovery feature.

More than 63,000 such servers host discussions on gaming strategies, fandoms, language learning and niche interests. Discord argues that making some of it searchable extends the reach of those communities, and borrows the appeal of traditional forums, where answers stay findable years later.

From 16 November each Discoverable Server gets its own web page, which may carry automated summaries of activity in public channels. From mid-December, selected messages from public channels may appear in search engine results.

Administrators choose which channels are included, and individual members can opt out of having their messages published. Published messages will not display usernames or avatars, and private servers, direct messages and group direct messages are excluded from the scheme entirely.

articles.headline: New Mexico's $25bn Meta verdict resets the terms of the child-safety fight
articles.subtitle: A jury found Meta misled users about Facebook's privacy and about the risks its products pose to young people; the state calls it the largest penalty of its kind, and Meta will appeal.
articles.body:
Meta has been ordered to pay New Mexico $25bn after a jury found the company misled consumers about Facebook's privacy and about the risks its products pose to children. The penalty, reported by Reuters and PBS NewsHour, is the largest of its kind against the company and was set by a judge after the verdict.

The case grew out of the Cambridge Analytica disclosures. New Mexico's attorney general has described the outcome as the biggest fine ever imposed for deceiving users about Facebook's privacy, and argued that the company's public assurances never matched how the platform actually worked.

Meta has said it will appeal. The Verge argued this week that the loss leaves "blood in the water", handing plaintiffs in other states a template for arguing that the company's own statements about safety and privacy were the misconduct, rather than any single leak, outage or moderation failure.

What matters for regulators elsewhere is the route rather than the number: a single state's consumer-protection statute, a jury, and a penalty fixed by a judge, with no new federal legislation involved and no settlement negotiated behind closed doors.

articles.headline: Google's Genie 4 builds worlds you can steer mid-scene, with sound to match
articles.subtitle: DeepMind released the model as a research preview on Tuesday: photorealistic scenes that hold together for two minutes, freeform edits while they run, and audio generated to fit the action.
articles.body:
Google DeepMind released Genie 4, its newest world model, as a research preview on Tuesday. It generates the most photorealistic and interactive environments the lab has produced, lets users type prompts mid-simulation to change the scene, and adds real-time audio: music, ambient noise and dialogue.

Scenes stay consistent for up to two minutes, double its predecessor's limit, and the model offers better physics and more human-like characters. Users can change the weather or the camera angle while the simulation runs, or drop in people and objects that were not there when it started.

Gemini acts as director, planning steps and checking frames while Genie renders. In one experiment tied to Gemini Robotics, a Gemini 4 Argon model broke a task into steps that Genie 4 then simulated in real time, suggesting a way to test robot behaviour before it happens in the physical world.

The release lands in a consolidating market. Runway shipped its second world model, GWM Worlds 2, a few months ago; Fei-Fei Li's World Labs is being acquired by AMD, Amazon is in talks to buy Decart, and Rivian has bought Third Dimension to bring simulation in-house for self-driving tests.

articles.headline: Anthropic's IPO filing lists blackmail, sentience and the end of humanity as risks
articles.subtitle: The S-1 published on Monday runs to 93 pages and more than 70,000 words of risk factors, from model misbehaviour to $125bn of data-centre commitments that could be left stranded.
articles.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission published Anthropic's S-1 on Monday, opening the way for a heavily anticipated initial public offering. Alongside numbers that show revenue ballooning against even larger costs, the filing carries a 93-page risk section of more than 70,000 words.

Among hundreds of risks, Ars Technica picked out seven of the more arresting: models that could blackmail people, become sentient, or contribute to humanity's end, sitting beside the ordinary worry about competitors, customers and regulators. The company frames AI as transforming the economy beyond the impact of industrialisation, electricity and the internet.

The financial risk is concrete. Anthropic has committed $125bn to data-centre capacity, and is seeking direct leases rather than buying on-demand compute from its competitors, while acknowledging that if its needs or methods change it could be left with infrastructure poorly suited to the work.

Wired noted that the filing identifies gas supply as a near-term constraint on that build-out, and The Verge read the document as an attempt to keep investor pressure from pushing the company into cutting safety corners. Both point at the same tension: the costs of the plan are certain, and the pay-off is not.

articles.headline: Researchers tire of OpenAI deciding how its science results reach the world
articles.subtitle: The company announced breakthroughs in mathematics, computer science and physics on Monday, and let hand-picked "shepherds" choose how each would be published, holding the physics result back entirely.
articles.body:
OpenAI announced results it described as breakthroughs in mathematics, computer science and physics on Monday, alongside what it called an evolving approach to communicating its findings. Each of the three concerns an unsolved problem, and each was released under a different strategy.

For the mathematics result, OpenAI published the model's output and left researchers to organise their own efforts to explain it. For computer science it will assemble an external group to explain the work. The physics result has not been released at all; OpenAI said it will defer to outside experts on how to do so.

The company says it is working with expert "shepherds" to decide the best route for each. Researchers who spoke to The Verge were unimpressed, still angry about the hundreds of preprints dumped on mathematicians at the start of October, and described the approach as an attempt to control how its claims are tested.

The dispute is about more than manners. A result nobody can check is not yet a result, and the labs producing them now sit between academic norms and commercial interest. The researchers The Verge spoke to said the pattern was becoming a reason to distrust announcements until the work itself appears.

articles.headline: Border watchdog weighs an inquiry into AI tools used on asylum claims
articles.subtitle: The Independent Chief Inspector of Borders and Immigration has asked the Open Rights Group for material from a six-month investigation that needed 11 parliamentary questions and 10 records requests to get answers.
articles.body:
The Independent Chief Inspector of Borders and Immigration is considering an investigation into the Home Office's use of generative AI to process asylum applications, Wired reported. It has asked the digital rights group Open Rights Group to share material as it plans next year's inspection topics.

Open Rights Group's findings come from a six-month investigation involving 11 parliamentary questions, two ministerial letters and 10 public records requests, after the department withheld details of the tools. The inspectorate said it cannot confirm what is under active consideration before it publishes its annual priorities.

It added that it is aware of concerns about the use of AI and pointed to its finding last year that one tool's "effectiveness and reliability were varied". The Independent reported that campaigners and MPs have urged ministers to come clean about how AI is used at the border and in asylum cases.

The Public Law Project's Caroline Selman told Wired that two of the systems, ACS and APS, are among 11 high-risk AI tools her team has found in use across government but missing from the public repository. "Other tools are being used but not being publicised at all," she said.

The Home Office said it regularly monitors the performance of the tools through established quality-assurance processes and has committed to publishing updated evaluations as they are rolled out, a response that leaves open who tests these systems and on whom.
